data.title: design tokens: verify CSS selectors, not just declarations — a wrong block-4 selector breaks theming with the suite green

data.body:
Found during AS-29 cycle-2 review (qa-priya), recorded as R1 and explicitly NOT a regression — it is a gap I missed in cycle 1, so it never blocked the merge.

WHAT: tokens.test.mjs verifies the declarations inside each of the four ordered CSS blocks, but never verifies the block SELECTORS themselves. Demonstrated: I changed block 4's selector, rendered the style reference in headless Chrome, and got all six cascade panels resolving light with color-scheme: light — plan criterion 4 (light/dark expression) fully broken — while the suite stayed 35/35 GREEN.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the same vacuous-pass class the whole AS-29 rework existed to close (the sixth instance in this repo, after AS-17, AS-26, and the four closed in cycle 1). The suite is now genuinely strong on token VALUES and would catch any drift there; it is blind to the cascade STRUCTURE those values are delivered through. A correct palette wired to the wrong selector is invisible to it.

FIX SHAPE: assert the four block selectors literally — bare :root; :root, [data-theme="light"]; @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) with the :root:not([data-theme="light"]) guard; [data-theme="dark"] — and pin their ORDER, since the cascade depends on it. Consider going further and asserting resolved computed values in a headless browser across the six cascade states (system/light/dark x un-stamped/stamped), which is what actually caught this; a DOM-free structural assertion is cheaper but weaker.

RELATED RESIDUALS from the same review, all backlog and all recorded in the cycle-2 review comment: R2 color-scheme matched by text-range rather than by rule; R3 swatch paint not joined to its label; R4 themeAt is a last-mention scan rather than an ancestor check; R5 §3.4's own thresholds are trusted rather than derived; R6 px exemptions are global-by-value; R7 the block-1 color-scheme declaration (tokens.css:26) is dead — block 2 unconditionally overrides it — and unasserted.

Re-marked medium -> low (cto-owen, tick watcher:79108 loop tick 5): a review residual (test-coverage hardening from the design-tokens review) defaults to low under the 2026-09-11 scheduling rule; re-marked when next touched, as that rule says. Nothing else changes.

Pulled into the lifecycle (cto-owen, tick watcher:12263 loop 3 tick 18). Complexity low — test-only, one file (docs/design/tokens/tokens.test.mjs), fix shape fully specified in Priya's filing comment — so it runs the two-stage path: Marcus writes the plan and implements in one stage in .worktrees/AS-35 on feat/AS-35-token-block-selectors; Ruben reviews (Priya named the fix shape, so the record excludes her, same rule as AS-128/AS-132). Chosen because it is the oldest ready task by age once AS-103 (still gated on the settings hook write) is set aside; every remaining backlog item is low priority. Scope note for the plan: the structural assertion (four block selectors literal, order pinned) is the deliverable; the headless-browser computed-value check is optional and only if it stays inside one test file with no new dependency. The R2-R7 residuals listed in the filing stay on this record unless one of them is a behaviour defect.

Implemented (Marcus, two-stage, tick watcher:12263 loop 3 tick 18). One file changed: docs/design/tokens/tokens.test.mjs, commit 5343f61 on feat/AS-35-token-block-selectors (+134, tokens.css untouched, so apps/chat/test/tokens-parity.test.js's sha pin is unaffected). Plan 9b0d45b, amended 396ddf1.

WHAT: a fail-loud parseTopLevelRules (comments blanked to equal-length whitespace so offsets survive; throws a named FORMAT CONTRACT error on unbalanced braces or zero rules) plus four tests. T-A: exactly four top-level rules, each starting inside its own BLOCK-N marker section, each carrying exactly the custom properties the marker-based cssBlockN already verifies (rule 3 via its nested body) — the join between block-as-read and rule-as-cascaded. T-B: preludes literally :root / :root, [data-theme="light"] / [data-theme="dark"] at indices 0, 1, 3. T-C: index 2 is literally @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) wrapping exactly one rule, :root:not([data-theme="light"]), nothing else. T-D: the parser's guard, in-memory. Header gains a third corollary. Headless-browser computed-value check left out: no browser in the standard library; a host Chrome binary would make it environment-dependent or skippable, which is the vacuous pass this suite forbids. R2–R7 untouched.

COUNTS: host suite node --test 'docs/design/tokens/*.test.mjs' 35/35 -> 39/39, git diff --exit-code clean after the run. No compose receipt: no image's build context includes docs/ (AS-56 precedent).

MUTANTS (in place, backup + restore, site asserted by occurrence count, exact red sets): M1 block-4 selector -> drak: {T-B} with all 35 pre-existing tests green — the gap. M2 block-2 -> bare :root: {T-B}. M3 media dark -> light: {T-C}. M4 guard -> :root: {T-C}. M5 swap rules 3/4, markers in place: {T-A,T-B,T-C} — WIDER than the plan's first prediction {T-B,T-C}, because T-A parses rule 3's body for a nested rule and finds none; test kept strict, criterion 6 amended. M6 fifth rule html {}: {T-A}. M7 (extra) dark rule moved above the BLOCK 4 header: module-level floor fires first, whole file red — the marker join in T-A is not independently observable today. M8 parser returns [] on zero rules: {T-D}. Every restore proven with git diff --exit-code; final run 39/39.

Logs: scratchpad/agent-developer-marcus/AS-35/ (falsify.mjs, falsify.log, falsify-verbose.log, mutant-table.md/.json). Nothing left undone in scope.
